questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) MODIFIED LANGUAGE READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used.
The DNA of prokaryotes is naked and circular. Which statement describes how the DNA of eukaryotes differs from that of prokaryotes?

options.A: It has a nuclear envelope around it and is a double helix.
options.B: It has a nuclear envelope around it and is circular.
options.C: It has proteins attached to it and is a double helix.
options.D: It has proteins attached to it and is linear.

options.C: the Mimivirus, but not the Pandoravirus
options.D: the Pandoravirus, but not the Mimivirus

questions.questionText: The diagram shows part of the organisation of a DNA molecule and the associated histones. P Q R Which statement about the features labelled P, Q and R during prophase of mitosis is correct?

options.A: The coiled DNA molecule forms Q and wraps around the histones of R to form small clusters held in place by histone P.
options.B: The groups of histones, P, and its associated DNA, Q, move closer together as the chromosome condenses around R.
options.C: The histones P and R are made of protein around which the DNA molecule, Q, is wrapped so that the DNA molecule can fit inside the nucleus.
options.D: The linked groups of histones P and R and the associated DNA, Q, form strands that fold and twist together to form a chromatid.
